title: Ha Lenne Időm... – Real vs. Hypothetical Ha

sections.title: The same ha, a different mood
sections.content: You already used ha with a real condition — Majd írok, ha lesz egy szabad hónapom (Unit 27) says something that might genuinely happen. A hypothetical ha sentence works differently: BOTH halves switch to the conditional, marking the whole idea as imagined rather than expected. Ha lenne időm, elmennék moziba doesn't promise anything about your afternoon — it paints a situation that isn't true right now.

sections.title: Real condition vs. hypothetical
rows: If I have time (and I probably will), I'll go.
If I had time (but I don't), I'd go.

items.english: If I had time, I'd go to the cinema.
If it rained, we'd stay home.
If it weren't raining, we'd take a walk.

sections.content: Both clauses take the conditional in Hungarian, even though English often keeps only one half in "would" — ha lenne pairs with elmennék, never with elmegyek.
